newsitem.title: MALDIVES: Pakistani PM confident India will discuss Kashmir.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani PM confident India will discuss Kashmir.

text.p: Pakistani Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif said on Tuesday he was confident India would agree to discuss the future of divided Kashmir in bilateral talks, and urged India to withdraw troops from the Himalayan region.

Sharif told Reuters Television before leaving a regional summit in the Indian Ocean island nation of the Maldives that he was satisfied with face-to-face talks on Monday with his Indian counterpart, Inder Kumar Gujral.

"I think the situation has taken a good turn. We have held talks yesterday after a deadlock of four years. The talks were very constructive, very meaningful, and we've agreed to talk more," Sharif said before boarding a plane.
Sharif said the Pakistani and Indian foreign secretaries would meet in Islamabad next month and hoped they would form working groups to discuss outstanding issues dividing the neighbouring countries.
Asked if one of the working groups should be devoted to Kashmir, the Pakistani leader said: "Certainly, because Kashmir is the core issue, and we have to address this issue very seriously."

Sharif was asked what would happen if India refused to discuss Kashmir in a working group. "I think they will listen to us," he said. Sharif was scheduled to fly to Iran to deliver financial aid to the earthquake victims, and then go to Turkmenistan later on Tuesday for a regional summit.
